model_annotation: Figure 3(a) illustrates the coverage metric as a function of the number of completions (k) for several Llama baseline models, both before and after fine-tuning on the distillation dataset. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” is on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Four distinct lines are plotted: a solid blue line with circular markers for “Llama-3B,” a dashed blue line with circular markers for “Llama-3B + FT,” a solid green line with triangular markers for “Llama-1B,” and a dashed green line with triangular markers for “Llama-1B + FT.” All lines show a generally increasing trend in coverage as k increases. For example, at k=1, Llama-3B starts at approximately 0.4 coverage and rises to about 0.75 at k=256; its fine-tuned counterpart begins slightly higher and reaches approximately 0.78. Similarly, Llama-1B starts near 0.35 and rises to about 0.7, while Llama-1B + FT starts near 0.38 and reaches approximately 0.72. The fine-tuned versions consistently show marginally higher coverage than their unfinetuned counterparts across all values of k, though the differences remain small.
